title: The square rule
tagline: Draw the box, skip the counting

principles.prompt: A pawn is running and your king is chasing. How do you know, without counting moves, whether you catch it?
principles.answer: Draw the square from the pawn to its promotion rank. If your king can step inside the square on its move, it catches the pawn.

principles.prompt: The runaway pawn is still on its starting square. What changes when you draw the box?
principles.answer: Its first step can be two — draw the square as if the pawn were already one rank further on.

principles.prompt: Why does it matter whose move it is in a pawn race?
principles.answer: If the pawn moves first, the square shrinks a rank before you can step in. Check the box you'll face after the push.

demos.title: Inside the box
demos.intro: The h4-pawn's square runs h4–d4–d8–h8. Black's king stands inside it — watch the catch run on rails.

steps.note: The king moves along the pawn's path, staying inside the box.
The pawn runs; the square shrinks to h5–e5–e8–h8. The king is still inside.
— caught. Inside the square at every step means the pawn never escapes.

demos.title: One file too far
demos.intro: Same pawn, but the king starts on c6 — and it's White's move.

steps.note: The pawn moves first. The square is now h5–e5–e8–h8; from c6 the king can only reach the d-file — one file outside.
Chasing hard, but the box has already moved on.
New square: f6–f8–h8. Still one file ahead of the king.
The king arrives — a move too late to lay a finger on h8.
Queens. Whose move it was decided this race on move one.

tests.title: Into the box
tests.intro: The h-pawn is running and your king is the only thing that can stop it. Step into its square.

wrong.Ke4: It looks like the chasing diagonal, but count the box: after h6 the square is f6–h8 and from e4 you can't reach it. Enter level with the pawn or ahead of it — e5 or e6.
wrong.Kd6: Too slow a road — after h6 the square is f6–h8, and from d6 you'd still be outside it. Step into the square now, at e5 or e6.
wrong.Kd4: Backwards out of the race — the pawn runs h6, h7, h8 while you're still on the d-file.

hints: Draw the square: h5–e5–e8–h8. Which of your moves step inside it?
Ke5 or Ke6 — both enter the square, and once you're in, the catch is automatic.

tests.explanationAfter: From d5 only e5 and e6 step inside the h-pawn's square. Once you're in you stay in — every push shrinks the box, but your king is always within it, and the pawn is caught.

tests.title: Don't chase — push
tests.intro: Your king can't help the g-pawn from back there. Does the pawn need help?

wrong.Kc2: Your king is a spectator in this race — while it strolls, Black steps into the square with Kd6 and the pawn is caught. Push!
wrong.Kb2: Your king is a spectator in this race — while it strolls, Black steps into the square with Kd6 and the pawn is caught. Push!

hints: The square of the g5-pawn runs g5–d5–d8–g8. Black's king is on c6 — what happens to the box if the pawn moves first?
g6 — the square shrinks to e6–g8 and Black is locked out for good.

tests.explanationAfter: After g6 the box is three by three — e6 to g8 — and Black's king was never getting in. When the square rule says your pawn wins the race, it needs no escort: every king move you make is a rank gifted to the defence.

tests.title: The two-step
tests.intro: The b-pawn hasn't moved yet. Count its square carefully before you commit.

wrong.Kh4: You counted from b2 — but a pawn's first step can be two. Count from b3: the square's edge is the g-file, and h4 isn't on it. After b4 you never catch up.
wrong.Kh6: You counted from b2 — but a pawn's first step can be two. Count from b3: the square's edge is the g-file, and h6 isn't on it. After b4 you never catch up.

hints: The pawn is on its home square, so its first move can be two. Where does the box really start?
Count from b3: the square runs b3–g3–g8–b8. Step onto the g-file — g4, g5 or g6 all do it.

tests.explanationAfter: A pawn on its starting square gets a free extra rank — always draw the box from one square ahead of it. From b3 the square just reaches the g-file, so any step onto that file catches the pawn; both waiting moves on the h-file lose the race by a single tempo.

tests.title: Step into the box
tests.intro: Black's pawn is off and running. Your king is the only thing that can stop it.

wrong.Kf5: Right file, wrong rank — the pawn's box runs c4–f4 down to the 1st rank, and f5 is above it. After c3 you're two moves adrift. Enter at f3 or f4.
wrong.Kg3: One square sideways isn't one square closer — you're still outside the box, and after c3 it shrinks away from you. Step INTO the square: f3 or f4.

hints: The square of the c4-pawn runs c4–f4–f1–c1. You're one step outside it.
Kf3 or Kf4 — either one steps inside; after that you stay inside all the way to c1.

tests.explanationAfter: f3 and f4 are the only doors into the pawn's square — remember the box has a floor as well as a wall, so f5 is no better than g3. Once inside you stay inside: each push shrinks the box with you still in it, and the pawn is met on c1's doorstep.
